title: One whole prayer
hook: putting it together: dawn prayer, two units, start to finish
tomorrow: When you stop, and start again

segments.voice: Yesterday: tayammum, and how the prayer bends to the body: sitting, on your side, or by signs. Your line was the prayer fits you.

It's like learning a song one bar at a time. Fifteen bars, one a day: the intention, cleanness, a direction, five times, two words that open the door, the standing, the bow, the rising, the prostration, the sitting between, the testimony, the peace to both sides, the count, the schools, and the chair at the back. Today you hear it played through, once, from the first note to the last. The shortest of the five: dawn, two units. Today: fajr.
screen: `FIFTEEN PIECES, ONE A DAY.` → `ONE BAR AT A TIME.` → `NOW PLAYED THROUGH.`

segments.voice: It's still dark. The sky is only beginning to gray. That's fajr's time. The person has made wudu, is on a clean spot, facing the qiblah. In the heart, the intention: two rak'ahs of the dawn prayer. Hands rise. Allahu akbar. The door closes behind. Hands fold, eyes down. The Fatiha, then a short surah, recited aloud if leading, because the dawn prayer is one of the spoken ones. Allahu akbar, and the bow: glory to my Lord the Great, three times, settled. Rising: Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You be the praise. Allahu akbar, and down: forehead, nose, hands, knees, toes. Glory to my Lord the Most High. Up to sit: my Lord, forgive me. Down again, the second prostration. That's one rak'ah. Allahu akbar, up to stand, and the cycle repeats: Fatiha, a surah, bow, rise, prostrate, sit, prostrate. Then, instead of standing, the person stays seated for the tashahhud: all greetings are for Allah, peace on the Prophet ﷺ, peace on us and the righteous, finger raised for the witness. Then blessings on the Prophet and on Ibrahim. Then right: as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah. Left: the same. And it's over. Five minutes, maybe less. Before it come two voluntary rak'ahs, which the Prophet said, in Sahih Muslim, are better than the world and everything in it. Every piece you've learned, in order, before the sun is up.
screen: `STILL DARK. WUDU. FACING THE QIBLAH.` · `STAND, BOW, RISE, PROSTRATE, SIT.` · `ONCE MORE, THEN THE TESTIMONY.` · `PEACE, RIGHT AND LEFT.` · then, large: `EVERY PIECE, IN ORDER, BEFORE SUNRISE.`

segments.voice: If you pray, pray the two rak'ahs now, slowly, the way you've learned them, noticing each piece as it passes. If you don't, walk through the shape without words, standing or in your chair: raise your hands, stand, bow, rise, go down or lean, sit, go down again; then once more, then sit, and turn your head right, and left.
Fajr, the two-unit dawn prayer: takbir to taslim, every piece in order, the whole thing played through for the first time.
Your line: the whole thing. Tomorrow: what happens when you stop. Two weeks of prayer, done.

howItsDone: The dawn prayer, fajr, is two rak'ahs prayed between first light and sunrise, recited aloud when leading, and it is preceded by two voluntary rak'ahs, often prayed at home.

fork.setup: you've finished the second prostration of the first rak'ah of fajr. what comes next?
options: sit for the tashahhud and end
stand up for the second rak'ah
fork.reveal: you stand with Allahu akbar and repeat the whole cycle; the tashahhud and the peace come after the second rak'ah.

original.note: Arabic: the dawn prayer. fajr means dawn, the first break of light.

trapdoor: what you thought: Muslim prayer is a long, complicated ritual.
what it means: the whole dawn prayer is two rak'ahs, takbir to taslim, about five minutes.
what a scholar hears: the pillars in order, the jahri (aloud) recitation at fajr, and Muslim 725 on the two sunnah rak'ahs before it.
guess: the dawn prayer, two units before sunrise
the night prayer, four units after dark
the midday prayer said on Fridays
